description:
## Goal

Every value admitted by a runtime-dispatch list predicate must be checked against the complete list surface from which that predicate was projected. The permanent `FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP` instrument must detect a value whose head passes an emitted test while some later element lies outside every correlated list clause the body named.

## Current state

Audited against clean pinned `origin/main` at `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`.

List-head predicates have landed. `ListShapes` carries one head question per cons-admitting clause, and the three lowerings test list shape plus one head. This is exact on rejection but erasing on acceptance: a passing head says nothing about the tail.

The dynamic tripwire remains inert. `surface_membership::escaped()` re-asks only the tuple axis under `PositionScope::Lowered` and `PositionScope::Full`; every tuple position is now lowered, so those readings are identical. `matches_list_head` reads only the first element, and `RuntimeValueReader` exposes no list-tail reader.

The existing environment mode, reporting, abort behavior, RAII census, and interpreter observation point are already present and should be retained.

A scratch prototype against this pinned tree established feasibility and live signal. Adding a representation-owned tail reader, walking every element under `Full`, preserving one selected clause question across the whole list, and comparing the value's applicable runtime axes compiled successfully. It reported one escape in `dispatch_list_head_separates` under `arms:3` and one in `enum_predicate_search` under `arms:6`; settled order reported zero.

Claims based on fz-kdt.143 commit `d2a5f3510` are not current-state evidence here: that commit is a child of this pinned main commit, not its ancestor. Re-measure the population from the implementation's actual main baseline.

## Strategy

Give the interpreter-side runtime value reader a representation-owned list-tail operation.

Keep `PositionScope::Lowered` identical to emitted behavior: list shape plus at most one head load.

Under `PositionScope::Full`, verify that one correlated list-clause predicate admits every element. Do not allow different elements to satisfy different clause predicates; `[int] | [:ok]` must not claim `[1, :ok]`.

Apply the comparison to direct list-valued dispatch subjects as well as lists reached recursively through shaped values. Keep the check behind the existing environment gate so the unset path pays no traversal cost.

Fold in fz-kdt.135's remaining corpus-sweep integration and triage. Record findings by fixture, permutation setting, dispatch, and predicate rather than blessing a count alone.

## Signal

- Unit tests distinguish emitted head admission from full-list membership.
- `[1, :ok]` passes the lowered `[int]` question but fails its full reading.
- A homogeneous all-int list passes both readings.
- A union of list clauses preserves clause correlation across the complete list.
- Direct lists and lists nested in tuple positions are both observed.
- `dispatch_list_head_separates` under `arms:3` and `enum_predicate_search` under `arms:6` demonstrate that the instrument can fire on the production interpreter path.
- The unset mode remains silent and avoids tail traversal.

## Acceptance

- `FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=abort` fails at each verified list-tail escape.
- Report mode emits and counts the same findings without changing program output.
- Lowered matching remains byte-for-byte behaviorally equivalent to the interpreter and native emitted tests.
- Full membership walks the entire proper list using one correlated clause predicate.
- A settled-order and legal whole-arm-permutation corpus sweep is run and its named findings are triaged into existing or new owner tickets.
- Update `runtime_type_predicate` documentation and `.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md` to describe the now-live list-tail reading and measured baseline.
- Run focused unit tests, the affected fixtures under settled and arm-permuted interpreter modes, `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --lib`, and the fixture matrix.

comments.text:
NOW LOAD-BEARING, not just an enhancement (fz-kdt.138, ce6768af4).

fz-kdt.138 retired the Scope-A carve-out, so every tuple position -- the
list-bearing ones included -- is decided by all three lowerings. Those
positions were the ENTIRE gap between PositionScope::Lowered and
PositionScope::Full, so the two readings are now the same function and
`surface_membership::escaped()` is literally `X && !X`.

CONSEQUENCE: fz-kdt.135's tripwire still reads 0 corpus-wide, but it reads 0
BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by measurement. It cannot fire on anything until
this ticket gives `Full` content the lowerings do not have -- the list TAIL.
The head is exact on rejection and erasing on acceptance, so a full re-ask
that walked the tail would find residue no emitted test can see (fz-kdt.131
facet 3's two pairs, plus analysis-excluded heterogeneous traffic).

The PositionScope plumbing was KEPT rather than deleted, precisely so this
ticket has its seat; runtime_type_predicate.rs's PositionScope doc and
.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md's "The dynamic tripwire" both now say the
instrument is inert until this lands. That is the honest present-tense fact,
and it is also the argument for doing this one sooner rather than later: the
dispatch class currently has NO live dynamic instrument.

ABSORBS fz-kdt.135 (2026-09-02): the corpus-sweep integration and the triage of the surface-membership tripwire's findings are re-based on the list-TAIL reading, which is exactly what this ticket re-arms once heads carry predicates. The tuple reading has no gap left (119/138), so 135's original ten findings are closed; whatever the tail re-ask surfaces is triaged here.

Baseline note from fz-kdt.143's landing (d2a5f3510). The list-TAIL re-ask this ticket arms will find a SMALLER population than the pre-143 tree carried: every arm whose tail no test reads and whose stand-in the seat would never let it pass is gone from every callsite (corpus arm lines 126 -> 106 on 4 fixtures), so the tail-blind traffic left is exactly fz-kdt.131's facet 3 -- five pairs under the widest legal arrival, three at the settled one (enumerated on 131 today). dispatch_list_head_separates still carries a written-down reproducer, but its callsite now offers two arms ([:false | :true] and [int | :ok | :true]) rather than four; the [int] and [int | :ok] specializations remain in the artifact, reached by direct call edges from the callable-flow path. The tripwire will see [1, :ok] arriving at the [int | :ok | :true] body through the surviving arm, not at a [int] body through a dropped one.

title: Re-arm the surface-membership tripwire by comparing list-head admission with full-list membership
